utterance: Samuel, everything you've told me and what I've found when examining you points strongly to appendicitis – an inflamed appendix. The pain starting around your belly button and moving to the lower right, the loss of appetite, feeling sick, the mild fever, and the way it hurts with every bump and cough are all classic for it. This isn't a stomach bug, and it won't settle on its own; it needs to be assessed by the surgeons at the hospital today, and it's most likely you'll need an operation to remove the appendix. That's a very common and safe procedure, and the sooner it's done the lower the risk of the appendix bursting. From now on please don't eat or drink anything, in case you need an anaesthetic. Do you have someone who can drive you to the emergency department right now? You shouldn't drive yourself.
reply: Can't I just go home and wait for it to pass?

utterance: I understand that's tempting, but no – this is one you really can't wait out. An inflamed appendix doesn't settle by itself; if it's left it can burst, usually within a day or two, and that spills infection into the belly and turns a straightforward operation into a serious, life-threatening illness with a much longer hospital stay. You've already had it for fourteen hours. You're young and otherwise well, so if we get you seen today you'll most likely have a quick keyhole operation and be home in a day or two. I'm going to phone the emergency department now so they're expecting you. Is there someone who can drive you there straight away?
reply: Yeah, my mate is outside in the truck, I can call him.
